relationship.claim: The Army awarded and administered the Camp East Montana task order on ICE’s behalf, then transferred contract administration to ICE effective October 1, 2025.

counterevidence.statement: ICE supplied operational support and led oversight before formal administration transferred. Several subcontractors had detention experience despite the prime lacking it. Neither fact erases the documented contract connection.

limitations: GAO inspected underlying records; this ledger reuses its retained audit and source catalog, not a fresh independent contract audit.
Financial/custody outcomes and correction remain separate claims; no automatic causal inference from the 75-day award-to-handoff interval.

next_test.question: Does the original September 23, 2025 contract modification confirm the precise administrative functions and effective date of the transfer?
next_test.required_record: One publicly available original signed contract-administration modification.
next_test.stop_condition: Stop after that one record or an explicit access/missing-record outcome; do not treat unavailable as refutation.
next_test.supports_if: It names ICE as receiving administrator effective October 1 and specifies the transferred functions.
next_test.weakens_if: It materially narrows, conditions or contradicts the transfer as summarized by GAO.

ordinary_explanations.statement: Agencies cited expedited leadership deadlines and failed ICE procurement attempts; an available contracting vehicle offers an ordinary explanation for the interagency cooperation.

relationship.rest_until: Rest until the named instrument or a material correction arrives; no collection scheduled.
relationship.scope: Contracting and administration relationship at one facility. It does not establish that the Army controlled every detention action or that transfer remedied deficiencies.

supporting_evidence.statement: GAO identifies Army award July 18, September 23 transfer modification, and October 1 effective administration handoff. Existing CEM04/CEM09 expand RC-006 IC02/IC03 without replacing them.

time_scope.note: Award to administration handoff; ICE had an operational and oversight role before October. Not the duration of every continuing obligation.

relationship.claim: The September 30, 2026 ORA memorandum directs the Armed Forces Chaplains Board and its Executive Director under the ORA director, changing the Personnel and Readiness reporting baseline recorded in the April 24, 2024 instruction.

counterevidence.statement: The same memorandum protects conscience and forbids compelled religious participation. Those provisions constrain the claimed authority; they do not measure enforcement or undo the reporting change.

limitations: B03 is official indexed text only; O01 is a visually inspected public-mirror facsimile supported by transcription/index, not verified original-host byte identity.
The status documents what the retained records direct; it does not promote an instruction into observed implementation or a motive finding.

next_test.question: Does one operative implementing charter confirm the Board’s actual reporting path and any limits or changes to the September 30 direction?
next_test.required_record: One dated official ORA/AFCB implementing charter or superseding directive.
next_test.stop_condition: Stop after one authoritative document or explicit unknown; do not infer continued implementation from silence.
next_test.supports_if: It confirms the directed path with effective date and responsibilities.
next_test.weakens_if: It rescinds, qualifies or reallocates the reporting path; an administrative delay limits implementation only, not what the original memo directed.

ordinary_explanations.statement: Administrative consolidation of chaplain/religious-support functions is consistent with the memorandum’s stated remit; the reporting change alone does not identify coercive implementation.

relationship.rest_until: Rest pending an operative charter, superseding directive or source correction; no monitoring enabled.
relationship.scope: Documented formal reporting direction, with source-access limitations. Staffing, actual exercise of authority, assessments and career effects are not established by this edge.

supporting_evidence.statement: The earlier Board reporting baseline is under USD(P&R), with intervening personnel offices. Full original PDF was inaccessible in RC-005.

supporting_evidence.locator: Memo p. 2 Board clause; p. 1 direct-report clause
supporting_evidence.statement: Inspected memo facsimile places the Board and Executive Director under ORA; the ORA director reports directly without intervening authority. Original government bytes were not compared.

time_scope.note: Memo effective immediately; the baseline event is dated April 24, 2024. An unknown end is not a claim of permanent/current implementation.

relationship.claim: Hypothesis: individually identifiable ORA-linked spiritual assessment information could enter assignment, promotion or other career-selection decisions.

counterevidence.statement: FM 7-22 preserves self-selected/self-assessed participation without repercussions; the ORA memorandum includes conscience/noncompulsion protections. They are formal counterconstraints, not proof of practical enforcement.
The February 2025 leader-assessment proposal precedes ORA and was development language, not a mandatory service-wide career rule.

limitations: No target event, personnel-access authorization, selection rule or verified career outcome has been supplied. Missing public records neither prove the pathway nor conclusively disprove it.
Temporal proximity, organizational overlap, shared terminology and reused sources cannot promote this edge.

next_test.question: Does a dated official ORA-linked assessment instrument or data-access rule authorize identifiable assessment data to reach personnel-selection decision makers?
next_test.required_record: One official instrument/data-access specification with fields, recipients, permitted uses and date.
next_test.stop_condition: Stop after one qualifying public record or an explicit unknown/access-limited result. No private soldier records or belief dossiers.
next_test.supports_if: It explicitly connects individually identifiable assessment data to authorized career-selection access/use; still distinguish authorized access from an observed decision.
next_test.weakens_if: It explicitly limits data to confidential/self-assessed or nonidentifying aggregate use and bars personnel-selection access; that narrows the authorized path without proving no informal misuse.

ordinary_explanations.statement: Voluntary self-development, confidential pastoral support or aggregate resource planning could explain assessment activity without individual career selection. These alternatives must also be tested rather than assumed.

relationship.rest_until: Rest as hypothesized until a discriminating dated record arrives. Any newly observed target gets its own event and linked relationship under review; no Bee or model dispatch.
relationship.scope: A candidate data/decision path. No inspected record establishes a deployed ORA assessment, identifiable command access, or use in career selection.

supporting_evidence.statement: The memo establishes organizational capacity and an assessment remit, not a career-data path.

supporting_evidence.locator: Army article published February 21, 2025 about February 19 development meeting
supporting_evidence.statement: Earlier development language anticipates team/squad leader assessment; instrument, retention, refusal and career use are unverified.

time_scope.note: No observed target date or established operational interval. The February 2025 guide-development event predates ORA; it cannot be counted as implementation caused by the September 2026 office.

relationship.unobserved_target: No documented ORA assessment-to-career-selection event exists in the inspected archive. The target is a proposed personnel-decision consequence, not an invented historical event.
